page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs built on a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 16.0 GB of memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio alongside a large 480 MB L3 cache and hardware-level instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Local ephemeral storage is provided via a 118 GB NVMe SSD with Premium Storage capabilities, and no dedicated GPU is included.

In performance evaluations, the E2ds_v7 demonstrates solid single-threaded execution with a stress-ng single-core score of 2215.58, placing in the average benchmark category. Multi-core performance reaches 2263.98, bounded by the underlying single physical core. PassMark memory testing registers at 1927.71, while uncached large-block memory write bandwidth measures 12.15 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, small model (135M parameter) LLM text generation achieves 88.94 tokens per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 4.95 GB/sec and Redis SET performance records 4.01 million operations per second.

The E2ds_v7 offers high memory density relative to vCPU count, making it a cost-efficient platform for operations requiring high memory allocations without needing heavy multi-threaded compute. The bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage without separate drive attachments. Its key hardware constraint is limited parallel processing power due to the single physical core design. As a result, this instance is best suited for in-memory caching, small relational databases, light web services, and enterprise workloads requiring substantial RAM per core.
